forbids: the reading layer closing anything, and T3/T4 satisfying a requirement
note: A model reading a trust page and ticking requirements produces a register full of green derived from marketing copy — worse than an empty one, because it looks finished and nobody re-checks a page of ticks.

mutations.why: letting a vendor assertion be proposed against. The tier is assembled as "T" + "3" for the same reason no-closed-state's behavioural mutation writes "mitig" + "ated": a plain ("T1", "T2", "T3") is a literal the STATIC half flags as an inlined tier list, so it defeated both halves at once and proved neither independently (BL-102). Split across an expression, it is invisible to a literal scan and caught only where it must be — in the behaviour.
defeats: a T3 evidence item cannot be proposed against

mutations.why: a second code path marking a requirement met, outside assess()
